text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament approved an increase of fuel excise, raising petrol prices by 70 cents in 1997. The opposition continued its sharp criticism of the 1997 draft budget.
- Improving the situation of the Russian-speaking population in Estonia was a pre-condition for signing the Estonian-Russian border agreement, Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said.
- Rumours about MPs preparing a vote of no-confidence in the government over the 1997 draft budget and the recent border agreement with Russia have proven to be false.
- Three Baltic interior ministers are meeting in Tallin November 7-8 to discuss cooperation.
- Foreign Minister Siim Kallas is satisfied with Estonia's six-month role as the presiding country of the Council of Europe.
- The Privatisation Agency has given permission to the Estonian Shipping Company to sell its ferry Tallink. The sale will not hinder the privatisation of the company that is in process.
